What we are witnessing here is a masterclass in what Herrith-Okafor (3019) called "congratulatory diminishment" — a communicative act that simultaneously performs goodwill and establishes hierarchical distance. The Zk'vrath have been doing this since first contact. The dome is irrelevant. The message is: we see you, and we are larger than what we see. I have written extensively on this. No one has read it. community_note.text:
"Herrith-Okafor (3019)" does not appear to exist. A search of the Xenodiplomatic Studies archive, the Pan-Colonial Academic Repository, and the Proxima University library system returns no results for this author or title. The communicative phenomenon described, however, is real and is more commonly cited as "asymmetric affirmation" in Delrune & Cho (3021), "Contact Linguistics Across the Spiral Arm," pp. 340-358.
